title: Ops Seller Safety Net - Microdeck Iter 1
body:
Purpose:
Compact, speaker-ready microdeck to help sellers and field ops move stuck pilot/proof-of-value conversations to safe outcomes. Focus is on risk mitigation, rapid canary checks, and a short technical script for last-mile integration with minimal platform dependency. Iter 1 is intentionally terse — keep it 6 slides worth of content in a single doc for rapid editing and printing as pocket-cards.

Audience:
- Sales Engineers (SEs) and Platform Sellers doing 30–90 minute pilot on-ramps
- Customer Success / Field Ops supporting activation

One-line pitch for seller to use on-call / handoff: "If the pilot hits latency or cost surprises, use the Safety Net script: reduce model footprint, enable prefix caching, and flip to a verified fallback — we’ll run the canary and confirm in 10–15 minutes."

Slide 1 — Problem + Quick Impact Statements:
- Problem: Pilots stall when SLOs and cost diverge vs expectations (esp. complex prompt systems, long contexts).
- Impact: Deals at risk, engineering time balloon, platform credibility hit.
- Quick stats (talking points): typical pilot shows 2x cost bump at 8k sequence length; 40% of pilot rollbacks are due to unexpected p95 latency spikes.

Slide 2 — Rapid Qualification Questions (30s):
- Is this: high-throughput customer-facing latency (<250ms target) or batched offline embedding job?
- Typical payload size (avg token length)?
- Are you using multi-stage prompts / tool calling or single-turn completion?
- Any regulatory requirement forcing private deployment or VPC-only?

Notes to seller: these are triage questions to pick the right safety net path (latency-first vs cost-first). Write answers into the pilot ticket and tag JIRA-OPS-987.

Slide 3 — Safety Net Paths (decision map in words):
- Latency-first (customer needs quick interactive response):
  * Try: switch to lower latency model variant (same family, lower perplexity tradeoff)
  * Tactics: reduce max_tokens, enable streaming, lower beam/temperature defaults, pin KV-cache warmup for top-k prefixes
  * Ops check: run 20-request canary with target seq_len distribution (see Canary Script)

- Cost-first (volume/embedding workloads):
  * Try: enable quantized model or a distilled embedding model; enable batching and prefix caching; use cached embeddings for repeated queries
  * Tactics: memoize repeated queries, add client-side debounce, set quota guard rails in Console

- Regulatory/Isolated (private deployment needed):
  * Try: short-term hosted -> dedicated staging on same region; if sensitive, propose Private VPC pilot using weekend maintenance window

Slide 4 — Canary Script (10–15 min ops runbook)
- Preconditions: customer API key, representative prompt set (10–30 examples), target seq_len histogram from logs
- Steps:
  1) Create a canary route in Console: label `pilot-canary-{acct}`; set model to fallback variant; enable request logging + tracing.
  2) Run 20 synthetic requests mimicking 80/20 token distribution (sample from prompt set). Record p50/p95 and cost per request.
  3) If p95 < SLO and cost delta acceptable -> promote fallback to pilot route and continue.
  4) If not -> escalate to Platform SE and open JIRA-OPS-987 with logs attached.
- Quick checklist items to capture: client timeouts, network region, model variant, quantization flag, batch size.

Slide 5 — Objection Response Snippets (speaker notes):
- "We need the best LLM quality": "We can run a quick AB on 10 golden prompts (we do this in the canary) — if the fallback degrades meaningfully we escalate to model engineering and surface exact diff examples."
- "Latency is inconsistent": "We’ll pin a canary in-region and test with your access pattern; often region routing or KV cache warmup explains spikes. If it’s model-level we’ll swap to a low-latency variant for the pilot."
- "We can’t give sample data": "We can run synthetic proxies derived from your schema, or run an on-site Private pilot where we never ship logs out of your VPC."

Slide 6 — Next Steps / Handoff Template (copy-paste into Slack / ticket)
- Subject: Pilot safety-net activation — {acct} — {date}
- Short payload: "We ran Safety Net canary for {acct}. Route: pilot-canary-{acct}, model: {variant}. Summary: p50={x}ms p95={y}ms cost_delta={z}%. Action: promote fallback / open escalation. Logs: attached."
- Required fields for handoff ticket: owner, SE-runner, test-set link, console route id, baseline perf numbers.

Appendix — Quick Pasteable Canary Commands (for SE terminal)
- curl examples (short):
  * create route: curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/routes -d '{"name":"pilot-canary-{acct}","model":"rwd-llm-small-1","max_tokens":256}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer {token}'
  * run request: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -d '{"route":"pilot-canary-{acct}","prompt":"<example>","stream":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer {token}'

Open questions / TODO for iter 2:
- Add short schematic showing routing fallback (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and where billing changes occur.
- Validate the 2x cost bump stat with Product Analytics (ping product-analytics@redwood).
- Convert to pocket-card printable PDF with TL;DR on front, checklist on back.

Notes to self (voice of draft):
- Keep it concise — field people will print and carry.
- Focus on time-to-safe-state (target 15 mins).
- Avoid deep model nuance; escalate to ME/Applied ML when necessary.

References and provenance:
- internal slack: #pilot-ops (thread link to be added)
- JIRA-OPS-987: pilot safety net epic (tracking canary runs and escalations)
- GitHub PR: ops-playbooks/pull/42 (canary tooling scripts)

End of microdeck — feedback welcome.
